# Grimling

> Grimling is an open-source mod for Claude Code: a pane of pixel-art agent cards docked beside the chat. Pick a card, type the task, press Enter. Watch the agent work, message it, read its answer and add it to your prompt. Unofficial community mod, not affiliated with Anthropic. MIT licence (code); Grim and the sprite art are CC BY 4.0.

Site: https://grimling.dev
Source and issues: https://github.com/grimling-dev/grimling

## Install

In a Claude Code session:

    /plugin install grimling --marketplace grimling-dev/grimling

Or from a terminal:

    claude plugin marketplace add grimling-dev/grimling
    claude plugin install grimling@grimling

Then run /reload-plugins (or start a new session) and type /grimling. Needs Claude Code 2.1.312 or newer (the tested version). Mods are an early-access Claude Code feature. Tested on Windows 11 and Linux; macOS passes the test suite in CI but has not been tried live.

## What it does

- The Grimoire: a filterable grid of agent cards built from Claude Code's built-in agent types, your agent files in ~/.claude/agents and the project's .claude/agents, and any agent packs you add.
- Launch in one line: pick a card, type the task, press Enter.
- Live agent cards: message a running agent; read, copy or add a finished agent's answer to your prompt.
- Flow, Table and Mermaid views of who spawned whom.
- A usage meter built from your status line (context, plan limits, cost, model).
- Arena lite: two cards answer the same question with a known answer and are scored.
- Grim, the mascot, pops up when an agent finishes, fails or is stopped.

## Safety facts

- No network calls: the mod makes no network calls of its own. /grimling-feedback only opens a link in your browser after showing what it holds.
- Local run log: launches, answers, stops and scored fights are logged on your computer in ~/.claude/grimling/runs/, one file a day, redacted by default (log.runs: redacted, full, meta or off).
- Stop needs a confirm: stopping an agent needs your confirm in the pane, then Claude Code's own permission check.
- Agents it launches run in your Claude Code session, under your permission settings, and use your plan.
